How to Plan a Garden

Learn how to plan a garden by observing the space before buying plants. Start with the light, soil and available water. Think about the way you want to use the space and the time you have for maintenance. A useful garden plan connects these practical decisions rather than starting with a shopping list.

Observe light and soil

Record which areas receive direct sunlight and which stay shaded. Check how quickly water drains after rain. These observations help narrow the range of suitable plants. A small test area lets you learn how the garden behaves through the seasons before making a larger commitment.

Choose plants for the space

Look at mature plant size, seasonal interest and the care each plant requires. Leave enough space for growth, and consider what the garden will look like outside the main flowering season. A modest planting plan can be easier to maintain than a crowded collection of unrelated plants.

What should I plant first?

Choose a small number of suitable plants and observe their growth before expanding the plan.
